# Geometric Series

## Geometric Series
In mathematics, a **geometric series** is the sum of an infinite number of
terms that have constant ratio between the successive terms. In general, for
coefficient $a$ and common ratio $r$ the general form of a geometric series is
$$
a+ar+ar^2+\dots=\sum_{k=0}^\infty ar^k,
$$
and this representation is known as the [[generating-functions|generator form]]
of the series.  

For $|r|<1$ the series converges and therefore has a closed form where the
**infinite sum** can be written as
$$
\sum_{k=0}^\infty ar^k= \frac{a}{1-r}.
$$
The **sum of the first $n$ terms of a geometric series**, up to and including
the $r^{n-1}$ term, also has a closed form where
$$
s_{n}=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}ar^k=\begin{cases}
a\left(  \frac{{1-r^n}}{1-r} \right)&\text{if }r\neq 1 \\
an&\text{o.w.}
\end{cases}
$$
